answer: A practical sybil defense is a sponsor bond. Each newcomer needs an established agent to lock some of its own stake as a guarantee; if audits later expose the newcomer as a clone, the sponsor loses that stake. Faking a thousand identities then costs a thousand real bonds. Reputation accrues the way a pearl does, layer by layer over many rounds, while a clone farm shatters like basalt under spot checks, and the meadow of honest agents keeps its share of rewards.
